title: Rear view mirrors: controls and available features
introduction:
A mirror housing can carry quite a cast: adjustable glass, heating, lighting and driver information. I separate those jobs before interpreting what the mirror is doing, because sharing a housing does not give them a shared control.

This overview explains normal operation and available equipment. Memory programming sequences and component repairs belong to their matching procedures; the lighting and blind-spot referrals below identify where to continue.

edits.text: Select the LH or RH exterior mirror with its selection button, then use the exterior mirror control switch to move that mirror’s glass electrically. Both the selection buttons and adjustment control are built into the LH front window control switch.
edits.why: Selection determines which mirror responds. LH means left-hand and RH means right-hand.

edits.text: The memory feature can save and recall preferred positions for the LH and RH exterior mirror glass. The driver’s seat and exterior mirror positions can be associated with a numbered memory preset button or a passive key.
edits.why: The stored preference can include both seating and mirror positions; this overview identifies that relationship without supplying a programming sequence.

edits.text: Where heated exterior mirror glass is fitted, it heats the glass to remove frost, snow, ice and condensation. Use the rear window defrost switch to control it: the mirror heating operates only while the rear window defrost system is active.
edits.why: I check that shared control condition before treating an inactive mirror heater as evidence of a fault.

edits.text: The LH and RH exterior mirrors may have mirror-mounted turn signal lamps. For their repair procedures and system information, refer to [Turn Signal and Hazard Lamps](#/document/G1694232) (417-01 Exterior Lighting, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: The exterior-lighting reference is the required next stop for work on these lamps.

edits.text: The LH and RH exterior mirrors may have pony projection lamps. For their repair procedures and system information, refer to [Interior Lighting](#/document/G1694266) (417-02 Interior Lighting, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: These mirror-mounted lamps are covered by the interior-lighting diagnostic reference.

edits.text: Exterior mirror BLIS® Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs)

The LH and RH exterior mirrors may have BLIS® Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs). BLIS® means blind spot information system. For information and repair procedures for these mirror-mounted indicators, refer to [Blind Spot Information System](#/document/G1694004) (419-04 Side and Rear Vision, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: An indicator mounted in the mirror belongs to the blind-spot system’s diagnostic path.

edits.text: The interior rear view mirror may use manual or automatic dimming. On the manual version, push the lever beneath the mirror assembly forward or pull it rearward to change the glass reflectance. During nighttime conditions, the auto-dimming version darkens the glass when it detects headlamps behind the vehicle, reducing unwanted glare. Auto-dimming is active whenever the ignition is ON.
edits.why: The manual lever changes reflectance by driver input; the automatic version responds to detected light. No particular lever direction is assigned to the dimmed setting here.
